To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the elliptic and the triangular flow in Pb + Pb collisions at the LHC are well described by viscous hydrodynamics with a specific shear viscosity of η / s ≈ 1 / 4 π and that the initial conditions of MC-Glauber provide a better description of both elliptic flow and triangular flow than the initial conditions of the MC-KLN model.

a simultaneous comparison with both elliptic and higher harmonic flow from ( 3 + 1 )-dimensional hydrodynamics favors a low viscosity quark–gluin plasma, and that the magnitude of elliptic and triangular flows are well described with MC-Glauber initial conditions while MC-KLN initial conditions are disfavored.
the elliptic flow of charged particles at the LHC is well described with a small viscosity and the triangular flow is not, while the reverse is true in the case of RHIC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the hydrodynamic elliptic flow and triangular flow in lead-lead collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 2.76 TeV per colliding nucleon pair.
the hydrodynamic evolution of the quark-gluon plasma created in heavy ion collisions.
the development of a new approach for the study of the dynamics of the relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrodynamic description of the data is very good and the data is very well described by the MC-KLN initial conditions with a viscosity value η / s QGP = 1 / ( π R ) ≈ 0.1.

the hydrodynamic description of elliptic and triangular anisotropic flow in Pb + Pb collisions at LHC energies with the MC-Glauber initial conditions and η / s ≈ 1 / 4 π is in agreement with the data.

the hydrodynamics + MC-KLN initial condition model provides an adequate description of the data, but the model is underconstrained by the data and the hydrodynamics+MC-Glauber model also provides an adequate description.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LHC data on elliptic and triangular flows are well reproduced by viscous hydrodynamics with small viscosity, and that the initial state of heavy ion collisions is better described by the MC-Glauber model.
the LHC data are consistent with a small viscosity QGP and the initial-state geometry is consistent with MC-Glauber initial conditions.
the LHC data favor the existence of a small viscosity QGP and the initial conditions from the MC-Glauber model. [1]
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simultaneous comparison with both elliptic and higher-order flow harmonics can provide a more stringent test of the initial-state and the hydrodynamical evolution of the system.
